subtopics.name: Increased intracranial pressure and head injury

questions.stem: Highlight the abnormal cranial nerve findings.

segments.text: reads the clock with each eye
full eye movement, equal reactive pupils
cannot close the right eye; right mouth droop; right forehead does not wrinkle
weak gag, wet hoarse voice, coughs after water

rationale.correct: CN VII, IX, X and XII are affected; these lie close to the brainstem where the tumor was.

perOption.s6: A complete right facial palsy, including the forehead, is a peripheral CN VII injury.
perOption.s12: Weakness of the right hypoglossal nerve; the tongue points to the weak side.

columns.text: Ask the client to smile, close the eyes tightly and raise the eyebrows

perOption.b2:c: Affects tongue movement, contributing to but not causing aspiration alone.
perOption.b3:a: An eye that does not close dries out.

questions.stem: At 0100 the client tries to climb out of bed and pulls at the IV. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Stay and speak calmly, using the name
Ask a family member to sit in
Lower the bed and cover the IV site

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that affect the choice and monitoring of antiseizure drugs.

rationale.correct: Genetics, albumin, contraception and driving all change the plan.

perOption.r2: Low albumin makes the total phenytoin level misleading.
perOption.r3: Enzyme-inducing drugs make it fail; valproate harms a fetus.
perOption.r4: Driving must stop until seizure-free per local law.
perOption.r6: Reassuring; still relevant for drug choice.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues for antiseizure drug choice.

questions.stem: With low albumin, the corrected phenytoin level = measured level / ((0.2 x albumin) + 0.1). What is the client's corrected phenytoin level? Record your answer as a whole number.

rationale.correct: 8 / ((0.2 x 2.0) + 0.1) = 8 / 0.5 = 16 mcg/mL, which is within range. Raising the dose for the 'low' level would risk toxicity, because more drug is unbound when albumin is low.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Laboratory reference ranges as used in common NCLEX review texts; follow the facility's ranges
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

rationale.correct: Genetic and pregnancy risks rule out carbamazepine and valproate for this client.

perOption.r1:c2: HLA-B*1502 positive: high risk of Stevens-Johnson syndrome; also lowers contraceptive effect.
perOption.r2:c1: Highest risk of birth defects in someone who could become pregnant.

perOption.r3:c1: Few interactions; watch mood and irritability.
perOption.r3:c2: Few interactions; watch mood and irritability.
perOption.r4:c1: Usable with corrected levels, but it induces enzymes and has long-term side effects.
perOption.r4:c2: Usable with corrected levels, but it induces enzymes and has long-term side effects.

questions.stem: Levetiracetam is chosen. Which teaching should the plan include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Take the medicine every day at the same times, even when well
Report new depression, anger or thoughts of self-harm
Do not drive until seizure-free for the period the law requires
Stop the medicine at once if a rash appears and seizures are rare
Take a bath alone to relax

rationale.correct: Teaching covers adherence, mood changes, driving, triggers and water safety.

perOption.c: Safety for the client and others.
perOption.e: Stopping suddenly can trigger status epilepticus; call first.
perOption.f: Showers or supervision reduce drowning risk.

questions.stem: While the phenytoin is being tapered on the ward, the client has a generalized seizure in bed. Place the nurse's actions in order.

items.text: Note the start time and stay with the client
Turn the client onto the side
Lower the bed, pad the rails and move objects away
Give IV lorazepam as prescribed if the seizure lasts 5 minutes
After it ends, check airway, breathing, neurologic status and injuries

rationale.correct: Time it, protect, side-lying, benzodiazepine at 5 minutes, then post-ictal assessment.

perOption.c: Lets secretions drain and keeps the airway open.

exhibits.title: Neuro ICU, postoperative day 1
exhibits.body:
A 56-year-old client had a craniotomy yesterday to remove a tumor at the base of the skull near the brainstem. Cranial nerve assessment this morning:
CN II: reads the wall clock with each eye.
CN III, IV, VI: eyes move fully; pupils 3 mm, equal, reactive.
CN V: feels light touch on both sides of the face.
CN VII: cannot close the right eye fully; right side of the mouth droops; forehead does not wrinkle on the right.
CN VIII: hears a whisper in both ears.
CN IX, X: weak gag; voice hoarse and wet; coughs after a teaspoon of water.
CN XI: shrugs both shoulders strongly.
CN XII: tongue deviates to the right when protruded.

exhibits.title: Medical unit, night shift
exhibits.body: An 86-year-old client with moderate Alzheimer disease was admitted 2 days ago with a urinary infection. At home the client takes donepezil. In hospital, oxybutynin and diphenhydramine at night were added. Tonight the client is suddenly much more confused, picks at the bed sheets, sees insects on the wall, and dozes off mid-sentence, then becomes agitated. The family says the client usually recognizes them and chats.

caseStudies.title: New-onset epilepsy and antiseizure drug safety

exhibits.title: Neurology clinic and ward
exhibits.body: A 27-year-old client had two generalized tonic-clonic seizures this month. The client works as a delivery driver, uses an oral contraceptive and is of Han Chinese ancestry. The neurologist is choosing between carbamazepine, valproate and levetiracetam. The client was started on phenytoin in the ED last week.

caseStudies.title: Epidural hematoma with a lucid interval

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: A 22-year-old client was hit on the left side of the head by a baseball and was briefly knocked out. The client woke up, said they felt fine, and walked into the ED with a headache. While waiting, the client became drowsy and vomited.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
